findings.state: Default onboarding flow, step 5 (Your open deals): a deal is added with Stage = "Proposal" or "Verbal yes", setup is finished, and Deal Workspace (or any area that reads deals through it) is opened.
findings.current: DEAL_STAGES (draft.ts:29-36) offers ids prospect / discovery / proposal / negotiation / verbal-yes / unsure. roomStage() (draft.ts:44-46) only maps "unsure" → "discovery"; "proposal" and "verbal-yes" are written unchanged to localStorage (seed-writer.ts:171, key gtmos_deal_workspaces) and to the cloud deals table (cloud-mirror.ts:127, column stage).
findings.problem: "proposal" and "verbal-yes" are not Deal Workspace stage keys. The owning area's keys are prospect, discovery, evaluation, poc, negotiation, verbal, closed-won, closed-lost (src/deal-workspace/lib/deal-shape.ts:18-27), and both of its readers coerce any other value to "prospect" (asStage, src/deal-workspace/lib/deal-bridge.ts:39-42, used by legacyDealToDeal line 99 and dbRowToDeal line 145). So a deal the user entered as Proposal or Verbal yes is shown as "Prospect" in Deal Workspace, gets stage probability 0 there (STAGE_PROB.prospect, deal-shape.ts:52), is no longer recognised as a late-stage deal by the areas that test the stage (Getting to Signed lists only evaluation / negotiation / proposal / verbal-yes, src/getting-to-signed/lib/cross-room.ts:59-67; Call in a Favor and the related-activity card test for "verbal", src/call-in-a-favor/lib/recommend.ts:67 and src/lib/follow/follow-data.ts:289), and the wrong stage is then written back over the stored value when Deal Workspace mirrors its list (src/deal-workspace/lib/legacy-mirror.ts:28-33 via persistence.ts:23), so the stage the user chose is lost. Before that rewrite other readers disagree with each other about the same deal: Quota Workback weights raw "proposal" at 0.65 and "verbal-yes" at the 0.3 default (src/quota-workback/lib/coverage.ts:29-40,67-69). An earlier probe of these exact functions (onboarding-work/out-verify.txt, lines C0-C1 and 'C-cloud') recorded: stored 'proposal' → Deal Workspace stage 'prospect'; stored 'verbal-yes' → 'prospect'; I re-read each function at the cited lines. Present since the flow shipped (commit 293f27c, 2026-06-29); not caused by the language work, but it is wrong data on the main path of setup.
findings.governing: AUDIT_BRIEF §5 'Function' (stable keys, stored shapes, cloud columns; "a display label stored where a stable key belongs") and §4 (numbers and states come from the area that owns them). Owning contract: src/deal-workspace/lib/deal-shape.ts STAGE_IDS.
findings.proposed: Make roomStage() return a Deal Workspace StageId: change its return type to the owning area's StageId and map prospect → "prospect", discovery → "discovery", negotiation → "negotiation", "verbal-yes" → "verbal", unsure → "discovery", and proposal → "evaluation" (shown in Deal Workspace as "Solution Fit", the stage directly before pilot/negotiation). Keep the onboarding DealStage ids and diagnose.ts unchanged (they are only used inside the flow). The other stage readers have to accept the same keys, or a Verbal yes deal from setup is left out again: Getting to Signed's list does not accept "verbal" or "poc" (src/getting-to-signed/lib/cross-room.ts:59-67), Future Autopsy's routing tests "verbal-yes" (src/future-autopsy/lib/action-plan.ts:108) and Quota Workback's stage weights have no "evaluation" or "verbal" entry (src/quota-workback/lib/coverage.ts:29-40); route those three to their areas. OWNER DECISION: Deal Workspace has no Proposal stage, so the mapping of "Proposal" is a product choice (Solution Fit vs Negotiation); the alternative is to replace the onboarding stage list with Deal Workspace's own six open stages (Prospect, Discovery, Solution Fit, PoC / Pilot, Negotiation, Verbal Commit, plus "Not sure yet"), which removes the translation but changes the options the user sees and which stages diagnose.ts counts as late.

findings.current: Assuming you need about 3.5 times your target in open deals over each sales cycle, you'd want about {need} open deals at once. You added {have}. That meets this estimate. Quota Workback will show if your open deals drop below it. / That is below this estimate. Quota Workback shows how far short you are as you add deals.
findings.problem: Two problems. (1) The closing sentences say Quota Workback tracks this estimate. It does not: Quota Workback (and the Dashboard's "Pipeline coverage") compares stage-weighted pipeline with the ANNUAL target against a benchmark multiple that depends on deal size (3.5× mid-market, 5× at $200k deals; src/quota-workback/lib/coverage.ts and engine.ts benchmarkFor). The estimate here is 3.5 × the share of the target that falls in ONE sales cycle, counted in unweighted deals. Executed by this reviewer in an out-of-repo probe that imports the real modules (final-audit/onboarding-fable/probe/out.txt): target $1.2M, $200k deals, 90-day cycle, ten deals added → this screen says "you'd want about 5 open deals at once. You added 10. That meets this estimate." and the Dashboard then shows "Pipeline coverage 0.5× / 5× — weighted pipeline is below benchmark"; with 21 deals at $50k in negotiation the screen says the estimate is met and the Dashboard shows 0.7× / 3.5×. A first-time user is told they have enough and, one click later, that they are far short. (2) "3.5 times your target … over each sales cycle" compresses the calculation: most readers will take "your target" as the annual number just typed (which would give four times as many deals). The step also renders "about 1 open deals" when the estimate is 1 (for example when the cycle field is cleared).
findings.governing: AUDIT_BRIEF §4 'Numbers shown in more than one area come from the area that owns them'; COPY_STANDARD.md §21 (claims discipline) and §6 (state the calculation); ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/11_AI_PROMPT_AND_GENERATOR_REWRITE_SPEC.md rule 2 ('State calculations as calculations').
findings.proposed: Replace the template and the two endings (QuotaStep.tsx:69-78) with a stated calculation and no claim about Quota Workback's measure: "In one {cycle}-day sales cycle you need to close about {perCycle}. Assuming open deals worth 3.5 times that amount, you'd want about {need} open {deal|deals} at your typical deal size. You added {have}." followed by, when have >= need: "That meets this rough estimate."; otherwise: "That is below this rough estimate." and then always: "Quota Workback measures coverage differently: it weights each open deal by stage and compares the total with your annual target." ({perCycle} = annualQuota × cycleDays / 365, formatted as money; use "deal" when need is 1.) Keep dealsForCoverage unchanged. OWNER DECISION: replace the estimate with Quota Workback's own coverage figure (computeCoverage with the benchmark multiple) so setup and the Dashboard show one number; that changes what this step reports.
